title: The Playlist of Maple Street
premise: Wendell Ravensworth has spent three years perfecting invisibility at Maple Grove High, tracking the basketball team's suspiciously perfect stats from behind her clipboard. When her grandmother dies and leaves her a recipe box filled with coded instructions instead of recipes, Wendell discovers her grandma was a school board whistleblower who died before she could finish exposing a grade-fixing and recruitment-fraud scheme that still runs the school. Following the recipe trail forces Wendell into alliance with star player Theo Okafor—whose scholarship depends on the very lie she's unraveling—and puts her on a collision course with Coach Danner and board chair Patricia Voss. In the end, Wendell must choose between protecting Theo's future and publishing the truth at the state championship game, where she broadcasts the evidence to the whole gym, costing herself her anonymity but winning back her voice.
about_author: Ansel Blackwood is a former high school math teacher who spent a decade watching teenagers navigate the gap between what schools say and what they do. He writes in a converted garage in Vermont, where his own grandmother's recipe box still sits on a shelf, unopened.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her system of invisibility: the seat by the fire exit, the stats notebook, the carefully unremarkable life. She notices an anomaly in the team's eligibility records but files it away. Emotional beat: the comfort—and quiet loneliness—of being unseen.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. After Grandma Ruth's funeral, Wendell inherits the recipe box and finds index cards of coded instructions referencing names, dates, and amounts that are clearly not ingredients. The first card decodes to a bank record. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Card Number Three
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Decoding leads her to a storage unit with boxes of documents: altered transcripts, cash payments, recruiting violations going back fifteen years—including her grandmother's name as the original source. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear when someone else has clearly searched here first.

chapters.title: The Star Player Problem
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Okafor, the team's centerpiece, is being leaned on by Coach Danner to keep his grades 'managed' in exchange for his scholarship. He notices Wendell asking questions in the library archives. Emotional beat: the suffocating weight of owing your future to people you don't trust.

chapters.title: An Uneven Alliance
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell confronts Theo with evidence; he nearly reports her, then reveals his own secret—a falsified transcript he didn't know was fake until now. They agree to decode the box together. Emotional beat: wary trust forming between two kids on opposite sides of the same lie.

chapters.title: What Voss Buried
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The trail leads to board chair Patricia Voss, whose career was built on the championship dynasty Grandma Ruth tried to expose. Wendell finds a letter showing Ruth was threatened into silence weeks before her death. Emotional beat: rage, and the first hint this is bigger than grades.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone ransacks Wendell's locker and steals two recipe cards; Danner offers Theo a deal—deliver Wendell's notebook and his scholarship becomes untouchable. Theo stalls. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival, and the cost of either choice.

chapters.title: The Long Division
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell learns Theo met with Danner and feels betrayed; Theo actually copied the stolen cards before handing over blanks. They reconcile but realize the remaining cards point to one last piece of evidence locked in the school's records room. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of courage.

chapters.title: Championship Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During the title game, Wendell infiltrates the records room while Theo deliberately throws off Danner's script on the court. She finds the final card—the master ledger—but Voss catches her, offering silence in exchange for a full-ride anywhere she wants. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Everything On the Record
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell refuses the deal and uploads the ledger mid-game; the gymnasium screens flicker with the evidence as the crowd goes silent. Voss resigns under investigation, Danner is suspended, and Theo's real talent earns him a legitimate offer. Wendell, finally visible, signs her name to the story. Emotional beat: truth as liberation, not ruin.
